name: RevioReputation Reviews Widget and QR Code for Google
author: revioreputation

sections.description:
ReviewQR by RevioReputation puts the Google reviews you already have on your WordPress site, with your real star rating and review count. You set the widget up once in your ReviewQR account, paste its code into this plugin, and add it to any page with a block or a shortcode.

The free plan has no monthly view limit, so the widget does not switch off on a busy day.

What you get on the free plan:

  • One widget with unlimited views
  • Two layouts: badge and carousel
  • A QR code that opens your Google review form, to print for the counter or the table
  • No credit card

ReviewQR Pro is $9 a month, billed monthly, cancel any time. It adds up to 5 widgets, all six layouts (carousel, grid, list, badge, floating, wall), printable A4 QR posters and stickers, up to 3 locations, and removes the “Powered by ReviewQR” line.

Good to know before you install:

  • You need a ReviewQR account to create the widget. The plugin only places it on your pages.
  • Google shares five reviews of a listing at a time. The widget collects your newest five about every ten days and keeps the ones it already has, so the list grows over time. Your rating and total review count are the real ones from Google.
  • Every review stays in the language its author wrote it in. The widget’s own labels follow your site’s language.
  • On the free plan the widget itself shows a small “Powered by ReviewQR” line. It comes from the ReviewQR service, not from this plugin, and Pro removes it. The plugin adds its own credit link only if you tick “Credit link” in the settings, and that box is off by default.
  • There is no review gating. The QR code sends every customer to the same Google review form, which is what Google’s policies ask for.

Made by RevioReputation, a small team in Varna, Bulgaria. If something you need is missing, write to info@revioreputation.com and tell us.

External services

This plugin shows a widget run by the ReviewQR service. Nothing is sent from your WordPress database.

  • On pages that contain the widget, your visitors’ browsers load the script https://widget.revioreputation.com/widget.js.
  • That script asks https://revioreputation.com/api/v1/widgets/public/ for the reviews of your widget, using the public widget token you pasted. As with any web request, the visitor’s IP address and browser user agent reach our server.
  • If you tick “Credit link”, a link to https://widget.revioreputation.com is added under the widget.

Service terms: https://widget.revioreputation.com/terms/
Privacy policy: https://widget.revioreputation.com/privacy/
sections.installation:
1. Install and activate the plugin.
  2. Create your free widget at https://widget.revioreputation.com/ and copy its embed code.
  3. Go to Settings, then RevioReputation Reviews, paste the code and save. Just the token works too.
  4. Add the “RevioReputation Reviews” block to a page, or put [revioreputation_reviews] where shortcodes work.
sections.faq:
Is it really free?

Yes. One widget with unlimited views stays free. You pay only if you want Pro for $9 a month.

Where do I change the layout or the colours?

In your ReviewQR account. The plugin reads them from there, so a change shows up on your site without touching WordPress.

Can I show two different widgets?

Yes. Use [revioreputation_reviews token="your-second-token"], or set the token in the block’s sidebar. Two widgets need the Pro plan.

Why don’t I see the widget in the editor?

The editor shows a placeholder. The reviews load on the published page.

Does it slow my site down?

The script loads async in the footer, only on pages that have a widget, and it fetches reviews when the widget scrolls into view.
